title: Lampshade Studio
summary: Create procedural lampshades by setting a final envelope and varying form, texture and twist. Preview the shade and bulb fit, then export a print mesh or CAD body. The included grow-light chandelier workspace extends the same project into an assembly; it is separate from a finished, validated lighting product.
features: Final outside width, depth and height in mm; unlink width/depth for an oval.
Eleven forms with ribs/folds, woven relief, smooth and triangular-facet texture choices.
Silhouette, cross-section, belly/waist and twist vary proportions inside the envelope.
Dimensioned E27 bulb guides, orientation and radial clearance preview.
Hollow material body for CAD, or filled outer envelope for vase slicing.
STL, STEP and OpenCascade BREP; Parasolid requires a compatible licensed local NX installation.
Save/Open JSON, hosted NAS drafts and separate chandelier design controls.
workflows: Design a shade to a fixed size
Set Width, Depth and Height first; these describe the final outside dimensions including texture peaks. Unlink width/depth for an oval.
Browse forms and select a starting style. Changing the style preserves the envelope rather than silently changing the final size.
Adjust texture, twist and profile. Values marked mm* are source-profile proportions before fitting, not necessarily final rim diameters.
Orbit the model, compare Front and Top and inspect the box and bulb guides. A radial fit check is not a heat rating or a complete holder-fit check.
Choose Solid envelope and STL. Select Lite, Balanced or Fine mesh detail according to the intended print and file size.
Import into the slicer as millimetres. For an open sleeve, use the intended spiral-vase setup and inspect zero top/bottom layers, perimeter and toolpath.
Inspect overhangs and the complete sliced preview. The preview shows a sleeve but the exported solid envelope intentionally has caps for the slicer to interpret.
Save the JSON separately so you can regenerate another size. STL does not contain the procedural design controls.
Choose Hollow shade when you want a material body to add mounting details to in CAD. The wall control is radial, not uniform surface-normal thickness.
Export STEP or BREP and wait for the server’s geometry checks. Complex surface combinations may take longer than STL.
Import the result into CAD, inspect bounds and openings, then add your fittings. The imported body has surfaces, not the original generator feature history.
Parasolid options require the local NX translator and licence; disabled NAS options are expected when NX is absent.
limits: CAD validity and dimensions do not certify a physical print, mounting system or thermal safety. No new physical print or heat test was performed. Third-party reference designs and libraries retain their own rights.
